correctness.rationale: Jacobian partial derivatives force singular points onto the six coordinate edges, and the nonzero coefficients yield twelve distinct nonzero roots. An explicit tangent quadratic is nonsingular at each root, so they are ordinary nodes. Artin--Schreier equations give their Frobenius splits; the edge coefficient maps are independent bijections of the nonzero field, proving every census coefficient. Resolution replaces each degree-one or degree-two node with a rational smooth conic, giving the exact zeta quotient. The included Python code exhausts all 59,049 F4 presentations and all 64 masks in F4 and F8; no finite experiment substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: The six edges are a natural geometrically intrinsic feature of the tetrahedral 12-node quartic construction, at the known nonsupersingular upper bound. All 64 Frobenius-descent profiles are independently attainable over every finite field with at least four elements and every profile has a closed count for all powers of two. This furnishes a complete arithmetic stratum classification of marked presentations and determines the exact exceptional-divisor correction to the K3 resolution zeta function. This is more than a single negative test or arbitrary low-dimensional slice; it does not purport to classify isomorphism classes.
